q: Did the authors use an external test dataset?
hint: Look whether an independent dataset was used to test the model.

q: Did the authors report whether they used an existing model or developed their own?
hint: Look at the end of the introduction, aim is often stated there.

q: Did the authors report whether their [1] code, [2] model and [3] data is open source? If so, did they mention where to find it and is the link permanent?
hint: Typically at the end of the paper, there is a section 'Coda availability' or related.
Are computational resources described (GPU, operating system, ...)? Is the data and openness described in sufficient detail?

q: Was transfer learning applied, and if so, accurately described?
hint: If TL was performed, is there a permanent link to the original and/or updated model?

q: Are all hyperparameters for model training specified to allow reproducibility?
hint: These can be many! To verify whether the authors did this, check for some that are very common, e.g. learning rate, train/val split ratio, early stop criterion, ...

q: Did the authors use other performance metrics than the most obvious ones?
hint: Accuracy and AUC are typically mentioned for classification, MAE / MSE for regression. It however doesn't allow a full appreciation of model performance.

q: Did the authors go beyond performance to assess explainability / interpretability / transparency of the model? (XAI)
hint: Might be in the methods or could also pop up in the discussion. This step aims to relieve the rat race on solely model performance.

q: Did the authors report on missing data and how it was handled?
hint: Missing data should be transparently described in the methods to avoid a potential bias during model training.

q: Did the authors report their rationale for using AI?
hint: Not every method calls for brute AI force. Were the authors mindful about their use for AI?

q: In case of classification, did the authors report on class imbalance?
hint: Class imbalance might drive model bias. In a dataset with 99 people with MS and 1 healthy control, a model that always predicts 'MS' is 99% accurate.

q: Is it immediately clear from the title that this paper involves AI?
hint: For later (systematic) reviews and immediate transparency on the use of AI.

q: Was the specific type of AI elaborated on?
hint: For example, unsupervised / supervised / reinforcement, expert-encoded system, which type of machine learning method, ...
